entries.text: The rules are conservative by design: they under-recommend rather than propose something clever and fragile, so a well-tuned network often gets no suggestions at all — intended, not a bug. Scope of v0

entries.title: UniFi integration
entries.text: Connect a UniFi controller with a local read-only account, see which endpoints are polled and what is never read, or type AP details in by hand instead.

entries.title: Create a local read-only account
entries.text: Do not reuse your administrator account. Make a dedicated account with the smallest set of rights that still lets it list devices, and treat the password as a credential for this tool alone. Settings

entries.title: Point the tool at your controller
entries.text: The URL depends on what you are running. A self-hosted software controller on a Linux host normally answers on port 8443: [unifi] host = "https://<CONTROLLER>:8443" site = "default" username = "wifi-s

entries.title: What is read, and what never is
entries.text: The integration reads inventory and counters: device models, firmware versions, channels, widths, transmit power, client associations, RSSI values and SSID names. That is enough to fill in the access

entries.title: Where the credentials live
entries.text: Controller credentials are stored in /etc/wifisurvey/config.toml with mode 0600 , owned by the service user. Nothing in that file is served over HTTP, and the API never echoes a password back. The ses

entries.title: Manual mode
entries.text: Manual mode is the default and it is not a degraded experience. You add each access point yourself: name, model, band, channel, width and transmit power. The tool uses that to place the AP on the plan

entries.title: Limits
entries.text: UniFi OS and the older self-hosted controller differ in URL layout, login response shape and where the network application is mounted. Both are supported, but a mixed environment may need the prefix s
